task.title: Migrating to a multi-region HA deployment — architecture planning
task.goal: Migrate to multi-region with zero downtime, targeting RTO < 5min and controllable cross-region consistency

userStory.trigger: Leadership wants a multi-region migration plan within 6 weeks
userStory.goal: Pick one executable path under zero-downtime and cost constraints
userStory.reads: The agent's read on the solution space: a phased decision backed by principle, a tradeoff still in play, and a compliance prerequisite awaiting confirmation
userStory.acts: Adopt the decision and move it into scheduling / dispute the tradeoff / add a budget or compliance constraint

observablePrimitives.label: TCO estimate across the three options

toolCalls.summary: active-active dual-write has the highest TCO

nodes.title: From "all-in active-active at once" to "phased"
nodes.from: Full active-active dual-write in a single cutover
nodes.to: Phased: cross-region read replicas first, then introduce write arbitration
nodes.rationale: Read/write ratio 8:1 plus +40ms cross-region writes: read replicas first capture most of the availability gains, while the high-risk cross-region writes can be deferred and rolled out gradually.

nodes.title: Adopt the phased plan: Phase 1 cross-region read replicas + global load balancing

evidence.label: read/write ratio 8:1 → read replicas cover most traffic
phased TCO is markedly lower than active-active dual-write

nodes.title: Strong-consistency cross-region writes vs. eventual consistency + operational complexity
nodes.falsification: If the business can tolerate 50ms write latency, Phase 2 goes straight to strong consistency; otherwise use intra-region strong consistency + cross-region eventual consistency. It hinges on the latency tolerance of payment reconciliation.

nodes.title: Phase 2: introduce cross-region write arbitration (tentative)
nodes.falsification: The shape of Phase 2 depends on the real cross-region latency and failover-drill results after Phase 1 ships; locking it in now would be an early commitment.

nodes.title: Full active-active dual-write in one shot
nodes.reason: Write-conflict resolution is complex, the TCO is the highest, and it can't be rolled out gradually — the risk and cost are unacceptable.

nodes.title: Is cross-region data residency compliant?
nodes.needs: Confirm with legal whether the target regions meet data-residency requirements; this is a prerequisite for Phase 1 site selection.

outcome.label: Planning decision · Grounded
outcome.text: Adopt a phased migration: Phase 1 cross-region read replicas + global LB.
outcome.recommendation: Clear the compliance prerequisite first (see "Needs your call" below), then let Phase 1 metrics decide the shape of the Phase 2 write arbitration.

steps.label: Initial plan
steps.hint: Open by considering an all-at-once active-active dual-write.

steps.label: Inflection
steps.hint: Aha: read/write ratio 8:1 + cross-region write latency ⇒ switch to phased, and active-active dual-write settles.

steps.label: Decision crystallizes
steps.hint: The phased plan crystallizes into a grounded decision (0.78), reproducible by simulation.

steps.label: Prerequisite risk
steps.hint: Honestly leaves one open risk: data-residency compliance is a prerequisite for site selection.
